summary.plain: CYGNO is a directional dark matter project at Gran Sasso. A gas chamber of helium and CF4 turns particle tracks into light that cameras photograph, giving 3D tracks and their direction. A 50-litre prototype ran underground; a 0.4 cubic-metre demonstrator is being built.
summary.technical: CYGNus module with Optical readout: He:CF4 (60:40) atmospheric-pressure TPC with triple-GEM amplification and optical readout (sCMOS camera for X-Y, PMTs for the drift coordinate). PHASE 0: 50 L LIME prototype, commissioned overground at LNF and installed underground at LNGS in February 2022 (about 27 months of data in five shielding configurations). PHASE 1: CYGNO-04, a 0.4 m^3 back-to-back TPC in LNGS Hall F, under construction; PHASE 2 aims at O(30) m^3. Part of the CYGNUS proto-collaboration; INITIUM ERC grant.

technology.quote: CYGNO [1] employs a TPC filled with He:CF4 (60:40) at ambient pressure.
technology.value: He:CF4 (60:40) atmospheric-pressure gas TPC with triple-GEM amplification and optical readout (sCMOS camera and PMTs)
